newsitem.title: USA: Primark, Dow Jones to form service.
newsitem.headline: Primark, Dow Jones to form service.

text.p: Primark Corp and Dow Jones & Co said Thursday they have formed a joint venture to develop a real-time equities news information service in the United Kingdom and Ireland.
The new product, to be called Primark/Dow Jones Equities Service, is scheduled to be released in the first half of 1997.
The new service will be integrated with expanded Dow Jones news and the news services produced through its partnership with the Associated Press.
The service will offer global financial data, including quotes, earnings estimates, and historical economic and financial information to an audience of equity traders and investors.
The information will be available through workstations, digital data feeds and trading room systems, including those of Dow Jones Telerate, the companies said.

Primark and Dow Jones said future plans call for tailoring the product for distribution in continental Europe and to other parts of the world. They did not say how far in the future that planned expansion would take place.
Terms of the venture, which is subject to definitive contract and certain regulatory approvals, were not disclosed.
Primark Corporation, an information technology firm, is based in Waltham, Mass.
